nodes.text: Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a set of $n$ points such that all pairwise distances differ by at least $1$. Is the diameter of $A$ at least $(1+o(1))n^2$?

#670 : [Er97f,p.6] geometry | distances The lower bound of $\binom{n}{2}$ for the diameter is trivial. Erdős [Er97f] proved the claim when $d=1$. The quantifiers are slightly ambiguous, but likely Erdős had in mind the regime where $d$ is fixed and the $o(1)$ term $\to 0$ as $n\to \infty$ (perhaps at a rate which depends on $d$). This was disproved if $n$ grows with $d$ by Ho [Ho26] : there exist infinitely many $n$ and, with $d=n^2-n$, a set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ such that all pairwise distances differ by at least $1$, with diameter at most\[\left(1-\frac{1}{\pi^2}+o(1)\right)n^2\approx 0.898n^2.\] Proof expositions (0) If you would like to contribute an exposition of a proof related to this problem, please message a moderator or leave your exposition as a comment.
